category: PyAEDT: Analysis Setups, Sweeps, Optimetrics & Solving
description: Creating and editing HFSS solution setups of every type (Driven, Driven Auto, Eigenmode, Transient, SBR+) through create_setup and the SetupHFSS object, adaptive-convergence and advanced options (matrix convergence, multi-frequency and broadband adaptation, derivatives, expression cache, mesh link, continue-from-previous), frequency sweeps with sub-ranges, the analyze/solve_in_batch/submit_job family with HPC options, variations, profile and convergence export, and the Optimetrics wrappers (parametrics, optimizations, sensitivity, statistical, DOE).

tools.name: hfss.create_setup (setup_type: HFSSDriven / HFSSDrivenAuto / HFSSEigen / HFSSTransient / HFSSSBR)
tools.description: Create an analysis setup of the given type and return a SetupHFSS (or SetupHFSSAuto) object. Keyword arguments are the native property names of the setup template, so any adaptive or solver option can be fixed at creation instead of editing props afterwards; the type must match the design's solution type (Eigenmode designs take HFSSEigen, SBR+ designs HFSSSBR, Driven designs HFSSDriven or HFSSDrivenAuto).
tools.usage: setup = hfss.create_setup(name="MySetupAuto", setup_type=None, **kwargs)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Setup name (unique within the design).

parameters.name: setup_type
parameters.description: "HFSSDriven" (default for Driven designs), "HFSSDrivenAuto", "HFSSEigen", "HFSSTransient", "HFSSSBR"; None picks the type matching the solution type.

parameters.name: HFSSDriven kwargs
parameters.description: Frequency="5GHz", MaximumPasses=6, MinimumPasses=1, MinimumConvergedPasses=1, MaxDeltaS=0.02, PercentRefinement=30, BasisOrder=1 (0/1/2, -1 mixed), DoLambdaRefine=True, DoMaterialLambda=True, SetLambdaTarget=False, Target=0.3333, UseMaxTetIncrease=False, MaxTetIncrease=1000000, IsEnabled=True, SaveAnyFields=True, SaveRadFieldsOnly=False, UseIterativeSolver=False, IterativeResidual=1e-4, DrivenSolverType="Direct Solver"/"Domain Decomposition", IESolverType="Auto"/"ACA", AdaptMultipleFreqs=False, MultipleAdaptiveFreqsSetup, UseMatrixConv=False, PortAccuracy=2, SetPortMinMaxTri=False, MinTri, MaxTri, UseABCOnPort=False.

parameters.name: HFSSDrivenAuto kwargs
parameters.description: AutoSolverSetting="Balanced" ("Accurate"/"Fast"), plus a sweep block (Type, RangeType, RangeStart, RangeEnd, RangeCount).

parameters.name: HFSSEigen kwargs
parameters.description: MinimumFrequency="1GHz", NumModes=1, MaxDeltaFreq=10, ConvergeOnRealFreq=True, MaximumPasses=3, MinimumPasses, MinimumConvergedPasses, PercentRefinement, BasisOrder.

parameters.name: HFSSTransient kwargs
parameters.description: TimeProfile="Broadband Pulse", MinFreq, MaxFreq, MaximumPasses=20, plus the adaptive options; the transient time step and duration derive from the frequency band.

parameters.name: HFSSSBR kwargs
parameters.description: RayDensityPerWavelength=4, MaxNumberOfBounces=5, PTDUTDSimulationSettings, ComputeFarFields, plus the SBR+ frequency sweep block (RangeType, RangeStart, RangeEnd, RangeStep).

tools.example:
s1 = hfss.create_setup("Setup1", setup_type="HFSSDriven", Frequency="10GHz", MaximumPasses=15,
                       MaxDeltaS=0.01, MinimumConvergedPasses=2, BasisOrder=2, PercentRefinement=25)
print(s1.props["Frequency"], s1.name)

eig = Hfss(solution_type="Eigenmode")
s2 = eig.create_setup("Modes", setup_type="HFSSEigen", MinimumFrequency="2GHz", NumModes=5, MaxDeltaFreq=1)

sbr = Hfss(solution_type="SBR+")
s3 = sbr.create_setup("SBR1", setup_type="HFSSSBR", RayDensityPerWavelength=4, MaxNumberOfBounces=8)
tools.notes: Native: oModule = oDesign.GetModule("AnalysisSetup"); oModule.InsertSetup("HfssDriven", ["NAME:Setup1", "Frequency:=", "10GHz", "MaxDeltaS:=", 0.01, "MaximumPasses:=", 15, ...]) or InsertSetup("HfssEigen", [...]), InsertSetup("HfssDrivenAuto", [...]), InsertSetup("HfssTransient", [...]), InsertSetup("HfssSBR", [...]). Unknown keyword names are passed through and rejected by AEDT with a message in the log; the template list is in the PyAEDT SetupTemplatesHFSS page.

tools.name: SetupHFSS object (props, update, update_property, properties, enable/disable, delete, is_solved)
tools.description: The handle for an existing setup (from create_setup, hfss.setups, hfss.get_setup or hfss.design_setups). props is the native property dictionary that is pushed with update(); properties/update_property use the ChildObject API with GUI labels; enable()/disable() toggle the setup for Analyze All; delete() removes it; is_solved reports whether results exist; sweeps lists its frequency sweeps and get_profile() / get_solution_data() give quick access to its results.
tools.usage:
setup = hfss.get_setup("Setup1")            # or hfss.setups[0]
setup.props["MaximumPasses"] = 20
setup.props["MaxDeltaS"] = 0.005
setup.update()                              # or setup.update({"MaxDeltaS": 0.005})
setup.update_property("Max Delta S", "0.005")   # ChildObject form
setup.enable() / setup.disable() / setup.delete()
setup.is_solved, setup.sweeps, setup.name, setup.available_properties
setup.analyze(cores=None, tasks=None, gpus=None, acf_file=None, use_auto_settings=True, ...)
setup.get_solution_data(expressions=None, domain="Sweep", variations=None, primary_sweep_variable=None, report_category=None, context=None, ...)
setup.create_report(expressions=None, ...)
setup.get_profile()
hfss.setups / hfss.setup_names / hfss.design_setups / hfss.get_setups() / hfss.delete_setup(name) / hfss.active_setup

parameters.name: props
parameters.description: Dict of native names (Frequency, MaximumPasses, MaxDeltaS, MinimumConvergedPasses, PercentRefinement, BasisOrder, SaveAnyFields, UseIterativeSolver, IterativeResidual, DrivenSolverType, MultipleAdaptiveFreqsSetup, ...).

parameters.name: update(properties=None)
parameters.description: Sends the current props (or the given dict merged into them) with EditSetup.

parameters.name: update_property(prop_name, prop_value)
parameters.description: Sets one property by its Properties-window name through the ChildObject API.

parameters.name: hfss.active_setup
parameters.description: Get/set the name of the setup used as nominal by reports and post-processing.

tools.example:
setup = hfss.setups[0]
setup.props["MaximumPasses"] = 25
setup.props["MinimumConvergedPasses"] = 3
setup.props["SaveAnyFields"] = False           # matrix-only solve, smaller results
setup.props["UseIterativeSolver"] = True
setup.props["IterativeResidual"] = 1e-5
setup.update()
print(setup.is_solved, [s.name for s in setup.sweeps])
for s in hfss.setups:
    if s.name != "Setup1":
        s.disable()
tools.notes: Native: oModule.EditSetup("Setup1", ["NAME:Setup1", "MaximumPasses:=", 25, ...]), oModule.DeleteSetups(["Setup1"]), oModule.GetSetups(). Editing a setup invalidates its results. SetupHFSSAuto (from HFSSDrivenAuto) exposes the same interface with the auto-solver properties.

tools.name: setup.enable_adaptive_setup_single / enable_adaptive_setup_multifrequency / enable_adaptive_setup_broadband
tools.description: Switch the adaptive-frequency strategy of a Driven setup: a single adaptive frequency (classic), several discrete frequencies each with its own Delta S (Multi-Frequencies mode, good for multiband antennas and filters with widely separated bands), or broadband adaptation between a low and a high frequency where HFSS picks frequencies automatically (recommended for wideband devices and Touchstone-quality sweeps). They set the AdaptMultipleFreqs / MultipleAdaptiveFreqsSetup properties that are awkward to write by hand.
tools.usage:
setup.enable_adaptive_setup_single(frequency=None, max_passes=None, max_delta_s=None)
setup.enable_adaptive_setup_multifrequency(frequencies, max_delta_s=0.02)
setup.enable_adaptive_setup_broadband(low_frequency, high_frequency, max_passes=6, max_delta_s=0.02)

parameters.name: frequency / frequencies
parameters.description: Single value or list, as floats in GHz or strings with units.

parameters.name: max_delta_s
parameters.description: Delta S convergence criterion applied at each adaptive frequency.

parameters.name: low_frequency / high_frequency
parameters.description: Band edges for broadband adaptation.

parameters.name: max_passes
parameters.description: Maximum passes for the broadband setup.

tools.example:
setup = hfss.create_setup("Setup1")
setup.enable_adaptive_setup_multifrequency(["2.4GHz", "5.5GHz"], max_delta_s=0.01)

setup_bb = hfss.create_setup("Broadband")
setup_bb.enable_adaptive_setup_broadband("1GHz", "20GHz", max_passes=12, max_delta_s=0.02)
tools.notes: Native: props "AdaptMultipleFreqs:=", True, ["NAME:MultipleAdaptiveFreqsSetup", "2.4GHz:=", [0.01], "5.5GHz:=", [0.01]] or for broadband ["NAME:MultipleAdaptiveFreqsSetup", "Low:=", "1GHz", "High:=", "20GHz"] with "Maximum Number of Frequencies for Broadband Adapt" in Design Settings. Broadband is not available with Domain Decomposition in every release.

tools.name: setup.use_matrix_convergence
tools.description: Replace the single Max Delta S criterion with per-entry matrix convergence: magnitude and phase tolerances for all diagonal entries, all off-diagonal entries, or a custom list of S-matrix entries, plus a magnitude threshold below which phase is ignored. Use it when the quantity that matters is a specific coupling (isolation, a filter transmission) rather than the whole matrix.
tools.usage:
setup.use_matrix_convergence(entry_selection=0, ignore_phase_when_mag_is_less_than=0.01, all_diagonal_entries=True,
                             max_delta=0.02, max_delta_phase=5, all_offdiagonal_entries=True, off_diagonal_mag=0.02,
                             off_diagonal_phase=5, custom_entries=None)

parameters.name: entry_selection
parameters.description: 0 = All entries, 1 = Diagonal entries only, 2 = custom entries.

parameters.name: max_delta / max_delta_phase
parameters.description: Magnitude (absolute) and phase (degrees) tolerance for diagonal entries.

parameters.name: off_diagonal_mag / off_diagonal_phase
parameters.description: Same for off-diagonal entries.

parameters.name: ignore_phase_when_mag_is_less_than
parameters.description: Entries with magnitude below this value are checked on magnitude only.

parameters.name: custom_entries
parameters.description: List of [port1, port2, max_delta_s, max_delta_angle] for entry_selection=2.

tools.example:
setup = hfss.create_setup("Setup1", Frequency="5GHz")
setup.use_matrix_convergence(entry_selection=2, custom_entries=[["P1", "P2", 0.005, 2], ["P1", "P1", 0.02, 5]])
tools.notes: Native props: "UseMatrixConv:=", True, ["NAME:MatrixConvergence", "AllDiagEntries:=", ..., "MagnitudeMin:=", ..., ["NAME:Entries", ...]]. In Terminal designs the entries are terminal names.

tools.name: setup.add_derivatives / get_derivative_variables / set_tuning_offset
tools.description: Enable derivative (sensitivity) computation with respect to design variables during the adaptive solve. HFSS then produces dS/dvar and, when a sweep uses UseDerivativeConvergence, lets reports be tuned in real time for small offsets of those variables without re-solving (the Tune Derivatives slider in reports). set_tuning_offset applies such an offset to a report from a script.

parameters.name: derivative_list
parameters.description: Variable name or list of design-variable names to enable derivatives for.

parameters.name: offsets
parameters.description: Dictionary variable -> offset (with units) applied in the report's derivative tuning.

tools.example:
hfss["patch_l"] = "29mm"
hfss["patch_w"] = "38mm"
setup = hfss.create_setup("Setup1", Frequency="2.45GHz")
setup.add_derivatives(["patch_l", "patch_w"])
hfss.create_linear_count_sweep("Setup1", "GHz", 2, 3, 201, sweep_type="Interpolating")
hfss.analyze()
print(setup.get_derivative_variables())
setup.set_tuning_offset({"patch_l": "0.5mm"})
tools.notes: Derivatives are only computed for variables that move geometry or material values used in the adaptive setup; the Optimetrics Sensitivity study is the alternative that re-solves. GUI: setup > Derivatives tab.

tools.name: setup.enable_expression_cache
tools.description: Add report expressions (field quantities, S-parameter functions, far-field numbers) to the setup's Expression Cache so they are evaluated after each adaptive pass and, optionally, used as convergence criteria with their own relative or absolute tolerance. This is how a solve can be told to stop when the gain, the Q or an integrated field has converged rather than only the S-matrix.
tools.usage:
setup.enable_expression_cache(expressions, report_type="Fields", intrinsics="", isconvergence=True, isrelativeconvergence=True,
                              conv_criteria=1, use_cache_for_pass=True, use_cache_for_freq=True)

parameters.name: expressions
parameters.description: One expression or a list, e.g. "dB(GainTotal)" or a named Fields Calculator expression.

parameters.name: report_type
parameters.description: Category the expression belongs to ("Fields", "Far Fields", "Modal Solution Data", ...); list when expressions is a list.

parameters.name: intrinsics
parameters.description: Intrinsic variation string such as "Freq='2.45GHz' Phase='0deg' Theta='0deg' Phi='0deg'".

parameters.name: isconvergence / isrelativeconvergence / conv_criteria
parameters.description: Use the expression as a convergence criterion, relative (%) or absolute, with the tolerance.

parameters.name: use_cache_for_pass / use_cache_for_freq
parameters.description: Cache per adaptive pass and per frequency.

tools.example:
setup = hfss.create_setup("Setup1", Frequency="2.45GHz")
setup.enable_expression_cache(["dB(GainTotal)"], report_type="Far Fields",
                              intrinsics="Freq='2.45GHz' Theta='0deg' Phi='0deg'",
                              isconvergence=True, isrelativeconvergence=False, conv_criteria=0.1)
tools.notes: Native: setup props ["NAME:ExpressionCache", ["NAME:CacheItem", "Title:=", "GainTotal1", "Expression:=", "dB(GainTotal)", "Intrinsics:=", "...", "IsConvergence:=", True, "UseRelativeConvergence:=", 0, "MaxConvergenceDelta:=", 0.1, "MaxConvergeValue:=", "0.1", "ReportType:=", "Far Fields", ["NAME:ExpressionContext", "Context:=", "3D"]]]. Far-field expressions require an infinite sphere to exist.

tools.name: setup.add_mesh_link
tools.description: Link the initial mesh of this setup to the solved mesh of another design or setup (Mesh Link / Import Mesh): the adapted mesh of a source solution is imported, optionally with the target's own mesh operations applied on top and with port re-adaptation. Typical uses are starting a second frequency band from an already converged mesh, or importing the mesh of a parametric variant to avoid re-adapting from scratch.
tools.usage:
setup.add_mesh_link(design, solution=None, parameters=None, project="This Project*", force_source_to_solve=True,
                    preserve_partner_solution=True, apply_mesh_operations=True, adapt_port=True)

parameters.name: design
parameters.description: Source design name.

parameters.name: solution
parameters.description: "Setup1 : LastAdaptive" of the source; None uses its nominal adaptive solution.

parameters.name: parameters
parameters.description: Dict mapping source variables to values (None = nominal).

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: "This Project*" or the path of another .aedt file.

parameters.name: force_source_to_solve / preserve_partner_solution
parameters.description: Solve the source if needed and keep its results.

parameters.name: apply_mesh_operations / adapt_port
parameters.description: Apply this design's mesh operations to the imported mesh; perform port adaptation in the target.

tools.example:
hfss.duplicate_design("Band2")
hfss["f0"] = "5.8GHz"
s2 = hfss.create_setup("Setup5G8", Frequency="5.8GHz")
s2.add_mesh_link(design="Patch", solution="Setup1 : LastAdaptive", apply_mesh_operations=True)
tools.notes: Native: oModule.EditSetup with ["NAME:MeshLink", "ImportMesh:=", True, "Project:=", "This Project*", "Product:=", "HFSS", "Design:=", "Patch", "Soln:=", "Setup1 : LastAdaptive", ["NAME:Params", ...], "ForceSourceToSolve:=", True, "PreservePartnerSoln:=", True, "PathRelativeTo:=", "TargetProject", "ApplyMeshOp:=", True, "AdaptPort:=", True]. The geometries must be topologically identical.

tools.name: setup.start_continue_from_previous_setup
tools.description: Configure a setup to start from (or continue) the solution of another setup or design - the Start/Continue From option in the setup dialog - mapping variables by name or through an explicit dictionary. In HFSS this reuses a converged adaptive mesh and fields as the starting point, which shortens re-solves after small edits or when chaining setups.
tools.usage:
setup.start_continue_from_previous_setup(design, solution, map_variables_by_name=True, parameters=None, project="This Project*",
                                         force_source_to_solve=True, preserve_partner_solution=True)

parameters.name: design / solution
parameters.description: Source design and "Setup : Solution" string.

parameters.name: map_variables_by_name
parameters.description: Match variables by identical names; otherwise use parameters.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: "This Project*" or another project path.

tools.example:
s = hfss.get_setup("Setup2")
s.start_continue_from_previous_setup(design=hfss.design_name, solution="Setup1 : LastAdaptive")
tools.notes: Native: EditSetup with ["NAME:PrevSoln", "Project:=", ..., "Design:=", ..., "Soln:=", ..., "MapVariablesByName:=", True, "ForceSourceToSolve:=", True, "PreservePartnerSoln:=", True, "PathRelativeTo:=", "TargetProject"]. The option is most valuable in Maxwell transient; in HFSS it behaves like a mesh link plus initial fields.

tools.name: setup.add_sweep / SweepHFSS (props, update, frequencies, is_solved)
tools.description: The generic way to add a frequency sweep to a setup and edit it afterwards. add_sweep creates a SweepHFSS of type Fast, Interpolating or Discrete with any native property passed as keyword; the returned object's props hold the full definition (RangeType, RangeStart/End/Count/Step, SaveFields, SaveRadFields, InterpTolerance, InterpMaxSolns, InterpMinSubranges, EnforcePassivity, ExtrapToDC, SMatrixOnlySolveMode ...) and update() pushes edits. The create_linear_count/step/single_point helpers are shortcuts on top of it.
tools.usage:
sweep = setup.add_sweep(name=None, sweep_type="Interpolating", **props)
sweep.props["RangeStart"] = "1GHz"; sweep.props["SaveFields"] = True; sweep.update()
sweep.frequencies            # list of solved frequencies (after solve)
sweep.basis_frequencies      # frequencies with fields available
sweep.is_solved
setup.get_sweep(name=None) / setup.get_sweep_names() / setup.delete_sweep(name) / setup.sweeps
hfss.get_sweeps(setup) / hfss.existing_analysis_sweeps / hfss.nominal_sweep / hfss.setup_sweeps_names

parameters.name: sweep_type
parameters.description: "Fast" (reduced-order, few solves, fields at all frequencies), "Interpolating" (rational fit to tolerance, S-only), "Discrete" (solve every point, optional fields).

parameters.name: props
parameters.description: RangeType ("LinearCount"/"LinearStep"/"LogScale"/"SinglePoints"), RangeStart, RangeEnd, RangeCount or RangeStep, SaveFields, SaveRadFields, InterpTolerance (%), InterpMaxSolns, InterpMinSolns, InterpMinSubranges, InterpUseS, InterpUsePortImped, InterpUsePropConst, UseDerivativeConvergence, EnforcePassivity, PassivityErrorTolerance, ExtrapToDC, SMatrixOnlySolveMode ("Auto"/"Manual"), SMatrixOnlySolveAbove, GenerateSurfaceCurrent.

parameters.name: hfss.existing_analysis_sweeps
parameters.description: All "Setup : Sweep" strings plus "Setup : LastAdaptive", the values used by setup_sweep_name in reports.

tools.example:
setup = hfss.create_setup("Setup1", Frequency="10GHz")
sw = setup.add_sweep("Sweep1", sweep_type="Interpolating", RangeType="LinearCount", RangeStart="1GHz",
                     RangeEnd="20GHz", RangeCount=2001, InterpTolerance=0.25, InterpMaxSolns=500,
                     EnforcePassivity=True, SaveFields=False)
sw.props["ExtrapToDC"] = True
sw.update()
hfss.analyze()
print(hfss.existing_analysis_sweeps, sw.is_solved, len(sw.frequencies))
tools.notes: Native: oModule.InsertFrequencySweep("Setup1", ["NAME:Sweep1", "IsEnabled:=", True, "RangeType:=", "LinearCount", "RangeStart:=", "1GHz", "RangeEnd:=", "20GHz", "RangeCount:=", 2001, "Type:=", "Interpolating", "SaveFields:=", False, "SaveRadFields:=", False, "InterpTolerance:=", 0.25, "InterpMaxSolns:=", 500, "InterpMinSolns:=", 0, "InterpMinSubranges:=", 1, "InterpUseS:=", True, "InterpUsePortImped:=", False, "InterpUsePropConst:=", True, "UseDerivativeConvergence:=", False, "InterpDerivTolerance:=", 0.2, "UseFullBasis:=", True, "EnforcePassivity:=", True, "PassivityErrorTolerance:=", 0.0001, "SMatrixOnlySolveMode:=", "Auto"]) and EditFrequencySweep(setup, sweep, [...]), DeleteSweep(setup, sweep), GetSweeps(setup).

tools.name: sweep.add_subrange (multiple frequency ranges in one sweep)
tools.description: Append a further frequency range (linear count, linear step, log scale or explicit single points) to an existing sweep, so one sweep covers several bands with different resolutions - dense around resonances, coarse elsewhere - exactly like the multi-row frequency table of the sweep dialog. Single points can additionally save fields for later field plots at those frequencies.
tools.usage: sweep.add_subrange(range_type, start, end=None, count=None, unit="GHz", save_single_fields=False, clear=False)

parameters.name: range_type
parameters.description: "LinearCount", "LinearStep", "LogScale" or "SinglePoints".

parameters.name: start / end
parameters.description: Range limits in unit (end unused for SinglePoints).

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of points (LinearCount/LogScale) or step size (LinearStep).

parameters.name: save_single_fields
parameters.description: For SinglePoints: save fields at that frequency.

parameters.name: clear
parameters.description: True removes all previously defined ranges first.

tools.example:
sw = setup.add_sweep("MultiBand", sweep_type="Discrete", RangeType="LinearStep", RangeStart="1GHz", RangeEnd="3GHz", RangeStep="0.1GHz")
sw.add_subrange("LinearCount", 2.4, 2.5, 101, "GHz")
sw.add_subrange("LogScale", 3, 30, 20, "GHz")
sw.add_subrange("SinglePoints", 2.45, unit="GHz", save_single_fields=True)
tools.notes: Native: the sweep array gains ["NAME:SweepRanges", ["NAME:Subrange", "RangeType:=", "LinearCount", "RangeStart:=", "2.4GHz", "RangeEnd:=", "2.5GHz", "RangeCount:=", 101], ...]. Interpolating sweeps treat sub-ranges as one fit; Discrete sweeps solve every listed point.

tools.name: hfss.analyze options (cores, tasks, gpus, acf_file, use_auto_settings, blocking, revert_to_initial_mesh)
tools.description: The full argument set of hfss.analyze / analyze_setup beyond the setup name: number of cores, parallel tasks and GPUs for the solve, an .acf analysis-configuration file, whether the Auto HPC settings apply, non-blocking execution that returns while AEDT solves, and reverting to the initial mesh before solving. The same keywords exist on setup.analyze and on Optimetrics setup objects.
tools.usage:
hfss.analyze(setup=None, cores=None, tasks=None, gpus=None, acf_file=None, use_auto_settings=True, solve_in_batch=False,
             machine="localhost", run_in_thread=False, revert_to_initial_mesh=False, blocking=True)
hfss.analyze_setup(name=None, cores=None, tasks=None, gpus=None, acf_file=None, use_auto_settings=True, ...)
hfss.stop_simulations(clean_stop=True)
hfss.are_there_simulations_running

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Setup or Optimetrics setup name; None solves all enabled setups (Analyze All).

parameters.name: cores / tasks / gpus
parameters.description: Override the active HPC configuration for this run; tasks=-1 in batch mode means automatic distribution.

parameters.name: acf_file
parameters.description: Analysis Configuration File exported from HPC and Analysis Options; applied for the run.

parameters.name: use_auto_settings
parameters.description: Let AEDT choose how to distribute frequencies/domains (Auto HPC).

parameters.name: blocking
parameters.description: False returns immediately (AEDT 2023 R2+); poll are_there_simulations_running or use get_monitor_data.

parameters.name: revert_to_initial_mesh
parameters.description: Discard the adapted mesh and restart adaptation.

parameters.name: solve_in_batch / machine / run_in_thread
parameters.description: Delegate to solve_in_batch on the given machine (see that entry).

tools.example:
hfss.analyze(setup="Setup1", cores=16, tasks=2, gpus=1, use_auto_settings=True)

# non-blocking run with polling
hfss.analyze("Setup1", cores=8, blocking=False)
import time
while hfss.are_there_simulations_running:
    time.sleep(30)
print(hfss.get_profile("Setup1"))
tools.notes: Native: oDesign.Analyze("Setup1") / AnalyzeAll(); distributed runs use oDesign.AnalyzeDistributed(setup). Core/task overrides are implemented through a temporary HPC configuration; with a scheduler-launched session they must not exceed the allocation. stop_simulations aborts running solves (clean_stop keeps the current pass' results).

tools.name: hfss.solve_in_batch
tools.description: Save and close the project, run ansysedt -ng -BatchSolve on it as a separate process (locally or on another machine) with the requested cores and tasks, then reopen it. Batch solving avoids the interactive session's memory footprint and license type, survives a lost GUI connection, and is the recommended way to run long solves from PyAEDT on workstations and single cluster nodes.
tools.usage:
hfss.solve_in_batch(file_name=None, machine="localhost", run_in_thread=False, cores=4, tasks=1, setup=None,
                    revert_to_initial_mesh=False, blocking=True)

parameters.name: file_name
parameters.description: Project file to solve; None uses the active project (saved and closed first).

parameters.name: machine
parameters.description: Host name for a remote batch solve (needs the same AEDT version installed there).

parameters.name: cores / tasks
parameters.description: Passed as -machinelist/-batchoptions; tasks=-1 means auto.

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Restrict to one setup or Optimetrics setup ("Design:Nominal:Setup1" style qualifiers are built for you).

parameters.name: blocking / run_in_thread
parameters.description: Wait for the process, or launch it in a thread and continue.

tools.example:
hfss.save_project()
ok = hfss.solve_in_batch(cores=32, tasks=4, setup="Setup1")
print(ok, hfss.project_file)
data = hfss.post.get_solution_data("dB(S(1,1))")
tools.notes: The command line it builds is equivalent to ansysedt -ng -BatchSolve -Distributed -machinelist num=<tasks> -batchoptions ... project.aedt. The Python object is re-bound to the reopened project; handles to boundaries/setups obtained before the call stay valid by name.

tools.name: hfss.submit_job (cluster submission via .areg settings)
tools.description: Submit the project to a job scheduler (LSF, PBS, SLURM, UGE, Windows HPC, or Ansys RSM) through the Submit Job mechanism: a settings file (.areg) exported once from the Submit Job dialog defines scheduler, queue, product path and batch options, and the call returns the job id. Combined with Desktop.job_status / launch_job_monitor it gives a fully scripted queue workflow without writing scheduler scripts.
tools.usage:
job_id = hfss.submit_job(cluster_name=None, aedt_full_exe_path=None, nodes=1, cores=32, wait_for_license=True, setting_file=None)
hfss.desktop_class.select_scheduler(scheduler_type, address="", username="", force_password_entry=False)
hfss.desktop_class.job_status(job_id)
hfss.desktop_class.launch_job_monitor()

parameters.name: cluster_name
parameters.description: Head node / scheduler address as registered in the Submit Job dialog.

parameters.name: aedt_full_exe_path
parameters.description: Path to ansysedt on the cluster; default /clustername/AnsysEM/AnsysEM2x.x/Win64/ansysedt.exe pattern.

parameters.name: nodes / cores
parameters.description: Resources requested.

parameters.name: setting_file
parameters.description: Exported .areg file; None uses a default template that PyAEDT fills with nodes/cores.

parameters.name: wait_for_license
parameters.description: Add the -waitforlicense flag so the job waits instead of failing when licenses are busy.

tools.example:
hfss.save_project()
job = hfss.submit_job(cluster_name="hpc-head", nodes=2, cores=64, setting_file="C:/hpc/slurm_hfss.areg")
print("submitted", job)
print(hfss.desktop_class.job_status(job))
tools.notes: Native: oDesktop.SubmitJob(settingsPath, projectPath, design=None, setup=None) returning job IDs, plus SelectScheduler, LaunchJobMonitor, RefreshJobMonitor. Export the .areg from Tools > Job Management > Submit Job > Save Settings after configuring the scheduler once in the GUI.

tools.name: hfss.set_custom_hpc_options / hfss.set_hpc_from_file
tools.description: Programmatic control of the HPC and Analysis Options configuration used by solves: set_custom_hpc_options creates/updates a custom analysis configuration (cores, tasks, GPUs, RAM limit) and makes it active, set_hpc_from_file loads an .acf configuration exported from the dialog (machines list, distribution types, MPI settings) and activates it. Both persist in the registry like the dialog does.
tools.usage:
hfss.set_custom_hpc_options(cores=None, tasks=None, gpus=None, ram_limit=None, ...)
hfss.set_hpc_from_file(acf_file=None)

parameters.name: cores / tasks / gpus
parameters.description: Resources of the custom configuration.

parameters.name: acf_file
parameters.description: Analysis Configuration File (.acf) exported from Tools > Options > HPC and Analysis Options > Export.

tools.example:
hfss.set_hpc_from_file("C:/hpc/two_nodes_dist.acf")
hfss.analyze("Setup1")            # uses the loaded configuration
hfss.set_custom_hpc_options(cores=8, tasks=1)
tools.notes: Related: hfss.set_active_dso_config_name(product_name="HFSS", config_name="Local") switches between saved configurations; -batchoptions overrides everything for a command-line run.

tools.name: hfss.available_variations (nominal_values, variations, get_variation_strings)
tools.description: The object that describes solved and nominal variations of the design: nominal_values returns the dictionary {variable: [value]} that reports and get_solution_data expect (and to which Freq/Theta/Phi are added), variations(setup_sweep) lists every solved variation, and the helpers build the variation strings used by native calls. It is the bridge between Optimetrics results and post-processing.
tools.usage:
hfss.available_variations.nominal_values          # {'patch_l': ['29mm'], 'patch_w': ['38mm']}
hfss.available_variations.variations(setup_sweep=None, output_as_dict=False)
hfss.available_variations.get_variation_strings(setup_sweep=None)
hfss.available_variations.independent_variables / nominal_w_values_dict
hfss.get_nominal_variation(with_values=False)
hfss.design_variation(variation=None)

parameters.name: setup_sweep
parameters.description: "Setup1 : Sweep1" to list variations that have results for that solution.

parameters.name: output_as_dict
parameters.description: Return each variation as a dict rather than a list of "var='value'" strings.

parameters.name: get_nominal_variation
parameters.description: Native nominal variation string ("patch_l='29mm' patch_w='38mm'"), with or without values.

tools.example:
vars_ = hfss.available_variations.nominal_values
vars_["Freq"] = ["2.45GHz"]; vars_["Theta"] = ["All"]; vars_["Phi"] = ["0deg"]
rep = hfss.post.create_report("dB(GainTotal)", hfss.nominal_adaptive, variations=vars_,
                              primary_sweep_variable="Theta", report_category="Far Fields", context="3D")
for v in hfss.available_variations.variations("Setup1 : Sweep1", output_as_dict=True):
    print(v)
tools.notes: Native: oDesign.GetNominalVariation(), oModule("Solutions").ListVariations("Setup1 : Sweep1"). Variation dictionaries must list every independent variable; PyAEDT fills missing ones with nominal values when possible.

tools.name: hfss.export_profile / hfss.export_convergence / hfss.get_profile / hfss.export_mesh_stats
tools.description: Retrieve solver diagnostics for a setup and variation: the profile (per-pass timing, memory, element counts, machine info) as a .prof file or as parsed Python data, the convergence table (Delta S / Delta F per pass, converged flag) and the mesh statistics file. They are what a batch script logs after every solve to decide whether to accept results or increase passes.
tools.usage:
hfss.export_profile(setup, variation="", output_file=None)
hfss.export_convergence(setup, variation="", output_file=None)
profile = hfss.get_profile(name=None)          # dict of parsed profile trees per variation
hfss.export_mesh_stats(setup, variations="", output_file=None)
setup.get_profile()

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Setup name.

parameters.name: variation / variations
parameters.description: Variation string such as "patch_l='29mm'" or empty for nominal.

parameters.name: output_file
parameters.description: Target path (.prof, .conv, .ms); None writes to the working directory and returns the path.

tools.example:
hfss.analyze("Setup1")
conv = hfss.export_convergence("Setup1")
print(open(conv).read())
prof = hfss.get_profile("Setup1")
for variation, tree in prof.items():
    print(variation, tree.props.get("Elapsed Time", ""))
hfss.export_mesh_stats("Setup1", output_file="C:/work/Setup1.ms")
tools.notes: Native: oDesign.ExportProfile(setup, variation, file, overwrite), ExportConvergence(setup, variation, file, overwrite), ExportMeshStats(setup, variation, file, overwrite). The GUI equivalents are HFSS > Results > Solution Data > Profile / Convergence / Mesh Statistics.

tools.name: hfss.parametrics.add (variable, start_point, end_point, step, variation_type, solution, name)
tools.description: Create an Optimetrics Parametric setup that sweeps one design variable over a linear-count, linear-step, log-scale or single-value range, tied to a solution setup. The returned SetupParam can then receive more variables (add_variation), synchronisation between variables, output calculations (add_calculation) and be solved with analyze(); results are indexed by the variation values in every report.
tools.usage:
param = hfss.parametrics.add(variable, start_point, end_point=None, step=100, variation_type="LinearCount", solution=None, name=None)
hfss.parametrics.add_from_file(input_file, name=None)
hfss.parametrics.delete(name)
hfss.parametrics.setups          # existing SetupParam objects

parameters.name: variable
parameters.description: Design or project variable name.

parameters.name: start_point / end_point
parameters.description: Range limits (numbers in the variable's units or unit strings); end_point None with SingleValue.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: Point count for LinearCount, step size for LinearStep (unit strings like "0.5mm" accepted).

parameters.name: variation_type
parameters.description: "LinearCount", "LinearStep", "LogScale" or "SingleValue".

parameters.name: solution
parameters.description: "Setup1" (adaptive) or "Setup1 : Sweep1"; None uses the nominal setup.

parameters.name: add_from_file
parameters.description: Build the variation table from a CSV/TXT exported by the Parametric dialog (Import/Export variations).

tools.example:
param = hfss.parametrics.add("patch_l", "27mm", "31mm", "0.5mm", variation_type="LinearStep",
                             solution="Setup1 : Sweep1", name="LengthSweep")
param.add_variation("patch_w", "36mm", "40mm", 5, variation_type="LinearCount")
param.add_calculation("dB(S(1,1))", ranges={"Freq": "2.45GHz"})
param.props["ProdOptiSetupDataV2"]["SaveFields"] = False
param.update()
param.analyze(cores=16)
hfss.export_parametric_results("LengthSweep", "C:/work/sweep.csv", export_units=True)
tools.notes: Native: oModule = oDesign.GetModule("Optimetrics"); oModule.InsertSetup("OptiParametric", ["NAME:LengthSweep", "IsEnabled:=", True, ["NAME:ProdOptiSetupDataV2", "SaveFields:=", False, "CopyMesh:=", False, "SolveWithCopiedMeshOnly:=", True], ["NAME:StartingPoint"], "Sim. Setups:=", ["Setup1"], ["NAME:Sweeps", ["NAME:SweepDefinition", "Variable:=", "patch_l", "Data:=", "LIN 27mm 31mm 0.5mm", "OffsetF1:=", False, "Synchronize:=", 0]], ["NAME:Sweep Operations"], ["NAME:Goals"]]). Data strings: "LIN start stop step", "LINC start stop count", "DEC start stop count", explicit lists.

tools.name: SetupParam.add_variation / add_calculation / sync_variables / export_to_csv
tools.description: Methods of a parametric setup object: add_variation appends another swept variable (including DecadeCount, OctaveCount and ExponentialCount distributions), sync_variables links variables so they step together instead of forming a full grid, add_calculation registers an output expression evaluated at given ranges (shown in the Optimetrics results table), and export_to_csv writes the variation table for review or re-import.
tools.usage:
param.add_variation(sweep_variable, start_point, end_point=None, step=100, units=None, variation_type="LinearCount")
param.add_calculation(calculation, ranges=None, variables=None, solution=None, context=None, subdesign_id=None, polyline_points=1001, report_type=None)
param.sync_variables(variables, sync_n=1)
param.export_to_csv(output_file)
param.props / param.update() / param.delete() / param.analyze(cores=None, tasks=None, gpus=None, ...)

parameters.name: variation_type
parameters.description: "SingleValue", "LinearCount", "LinearStep", "DecadeCount", "OctaveCount", "ExponentialCount".

parameters.name: calculation / ranges
parameters.description: Report expression and dict of intrinsic values, e.g. {"Freq": "2.45GHz"} or {"Freq": ("1GHz", "3GHz")} for a range, {"Theta": ["0deg", "30deg"]} for discrete lists.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Infinite sphere name for far-field calculations, polyline name for field calculations.

parameters.name: variables / sync_n
parameters.description: Variables to synchronise and the synchronisation group number.

tools.example:
param = hfss.parametrics.add("theta_scan", 0, 60, 7, variation_type="LinearCount", name="Scan")
param.add_variation("phi_scan", 0, 90, 4, variation_type="LinearCount")
param.sync_variables(["theta_scan", "phi_scan"], sync_n=1)     # step together (7 runs, not 28)
param.add_calculation("dB(RealizedGainTotal)", ranges={"Freq": "10GHz", "Theta": "theta_scan", "Phi": "phi_scan"}, context="3D")
param.export_to_csv("C:/work/scan_table.csv")
tools.notes: Calculations appear as columns in the Parametric setup's View Analysis Result table and are also exported by hfss.export_parametric_results. Synchronised variables must have the same number of points.

tools.name: hfss.optimizations.add (optimization_type: Optimization / Sensitivity / Statistical / DXDOE / DesignExplorer / optiSLang)
tools.description: Create an Optimetrics setup of any non-parametric type in one call, with a first goal defined by a calculation, its ranges, condition, goal value and weight, and optionally the subset of variables to include. The returned SetupOpti exposes props for the optimiser choice and stop criteria, add_goal for additional goals and add_variation for variable bounds, and analyze() to run it.
tools.usage:
opt = hfss.optimizations.add(calculation=None, ranges=None, variables=None, optimization_type="Optimization", condition="<=",
                             goal_value=1, goal_weight=1, solution=None, name=None, context=None, subdesign_id=None,
                             polyline_points=1001, report_type=None)
hfss.optimizations.delete(name)
hfss.optimizations.setups

parameters.name: calculation / ranges / context
parameters.description: Goal expression ("dB(S(1,1))", "max(dB(GainTotal))"), intrinsic ranges dict, and context (sphere/polyline/matrix).

parameters.name: optimization_type
parameters.description: "Optimization", "Sensitivity", "Statistical", "DXDOE" (DesignXplorer DOE), "DesignExplorer", "optiSLang".

parameters.name: condition / goal_value / goal_weight
parameters.description: "<=", ">=", "==", "Minimize", "Maximize" with target and weight.

parameters.name: variables
parameters.description: List of variables to include (all activated variables by default); their ranges come from the variable's optimisation settings or add_variation.

parameters.name: solution
parameters.description: "Setup1 : LastAdaptive" or a sweep.

tools.example:
hfss.activate_variable_optimization("patch_l", "27mm", "31mm")
opt = hfss.optimizations.add(calculation="dB(S(1,1))", ranges={"Freq": "2.45GHz"}, variables=["patch_l"],
                             optimization_type="Optimization", condition="<=", goal_value=-20, goal_weight=1,
                             solution="Setup1 : Sweep1", name="MatchOpt")
opt.props["Optimizer"] = "Quasi Newton"          # or "Pattern Search", "SNLP", "Genetic Algorithm", "MATLAB Optimizer"
opt.props["AnalysisStopOptions"]["MaxNumIteration"] = 50
opt.update()
opt.analyze()

sens = hfss.optimizations.add("dB(S(1,1))", {"Freq": "2.45GHz"}, optimization_type="Sensitivity", name="Sens1")
stat = hfss.optimizations.add("dB(S(1,1))", {"Freq": "2.45GHz"}, optimization_type="Statistical", name="Stat1")
tools.notes: Native: oModule.InsertSetup("OptiOptimization", ["NAME:MatchOpt", "IsEnabled:=", True, ["NAME:ProdOptiSetupDataV2", ...], ["NAME:StartingPoint", "patch_l:=", "29mm"], "Optimizer:=", "Quasi Newton", ["NAME:AnalysisStopOptions", "StopForNumIteration:=", True, "MaxNumIteration:=", 50, ...], "CostFuncNormType:=", "L2", ["NAME:Variables", "patch_l:=", ["i:=", True, "int:=", False, "Min:=", "27mm", "Max:=", "31mm", ...]], ["NAME:Goals", ["NAME:Goal", "ReportType:=", "Modal Solution Data", "Solution:=", "Setup1 : Sweep1", ["NAME:SimValueContext", "Domain:=", "Sweep"], "Calculation:=", "dB(S(1,1))", "Name:=", "dB(S(1,1))", ["NAME:Ranges", "Range:=", ["Var:=", "Freq", "Type:=", "d", "DiscreteValues:=", "2.45GHz"]], "Condition:=", "<=", ["NAME:GoalValue", "GoalValueType:=", "Independent", "Format:=", "Real/Imag", "bG:=", ["v:=", "[-20;]"]], "Weight:=", "[1]"]]]); OptiSensitivity / OptiStatistical / OptiDXDOE use the same InsertSetup with their own arrays. A variable must be enabled for the study type (activate_variable_*) before it can be included.

tools.name: SetupOpti.add_goal / SetupOpti.add_variation
tools.description: Extend an optimisation, sensitivity, statistical or DOE setup: add_goal appends another cost-function term (expression, ranges, condition, target, weight, context), and add_variation adds a variable as an input with its minimum, maximum, starting value and step limits. Multi-goal optimisations (match at two frequencies, gain above a level, isolation below a level) are built by chaining add_goal calls.
tools.usage:
opt.add_goal(calculation, ranges, variables=None, solution=None, context=None, subdesign_id=None, polyline_points=1001,
             report_type=None, condition="<=", goal_value=1, goal_weight=1)
opt.add_variation(variable_name, min_value, max_value, starting_point=None, min_step=None, max_step=None, use_manufacturable=False, levels=None)
opt.props / opt.update() / opt.delete() / opt.analyze()

parameters.name: calculation / ranges / context
parameters.description: As in optimizations.add; ranges may give a frequency band as a tuple so the goal applies over the band.

parameters.name: condition / goal_value / goal_weight
parameters.description: "<=", ">=", "==", "Minimize", "Maximize"; target and relative weight.

parameters.name: variable_name / min_value / max_value
parameters.description: Input variable and its bounds (unit strings).

parameters.name: min_step / max_step
parameters.description: Step limits used by gradient optimisers.

parameters.name: use_manufacturable / levels
parameters.description: Restrict to a list of manufacturable values.

tools.example:
opt = hfss.optimizations.add("dB(S(1,1))", {"Freq": ("2.4GHz", "2.5GHz")}, condition="<=", goal_value=-15, name="Dual")
opt.add_goal("dB(S(2,1))", {"Freq": "2.45GHz"}, condition=">=", goal_value=-0.5, goal_weight=2)
opt.add_goal("dB(GainTotal)", {"Freq": "2.45GHz", "Theta": "0deg", "Phi": "0deg"}, context="3D", condition=">=", goal_value=6)
opt.add_variation("patch_l", "27mm", "31mm", starting_point="29mm", min_step="0.05mm", max_step="0.5mm")
opt.add_variation("feed_x", "2mm", "12mm")
opt.analyze()
tools.notes: Goals over a frequency band are evaluated at every solved frequency in the band (each point contributes to the cost). Weights are relative; the cost function norm is set by props["CostFuncNormType"] ("L1", "L2", "Maximum").

tools.name: hfss.activate_variable_optimization / activate_variable_sensitivity / activate_variable_statistical / activate_variable_tuning (and deactivate_*)
tools.description: Enable a design variable for a given Optimetrics study type and optionally set its range - the checkboxes and min/max columns of the Optimization / Sensitivity / Statistical / Tuning tabs in the variable's Properties dialog. Optimetrics setups only see variables that are enabled for their study type, so these calls come before optimizations.add; the deactivate_* counterparts remove the variable from the study.
tools.usage:
hfss.activate_variable_optimization(name, minimum=None, maximum=None)
hfss.activate_variable_sensitivity(name, minimum=None, maximum=None)
hfss.activate_variable_statistical(name, minimum=None, maximum=None, tolerance=None, probability=None, mean=None)
hfss.activate_variable_tuning(name, minimum=None, maximum=None)
hfss.deactivate_variable_optimization(name) / deactivate_variable_sensitivity(name) / deactivate_variable_statistical(name) / deactivate_variable_tuning(name)

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Design or project ($) variable.

parameters.name: minimum / maximum
parameters.description: Bounds with units; None keeps the current values.

parameters.name: tolerance / probability / mean
parameters.description: Statistical distribution parameters (tolerance in %, probability distribution, mean value).

tools.example:
for v, lo, hi in [("patch_l", "27mm", "31mm"), ("patch_w", "35mm", "41mm"), ("feed_x", "2mm", "12mm")]:
    hfss.activate_variable_optimization(v, lo, hi)
    hfss.activate_variable_sensitivity(v, lo, hi)
hfss.activate_variable_statistical("$sub_h", tolerance=5)
hfss.activate_variable_tuning("patch_l", "27mm", "31mm")
tools.notes: Native: oDesign.ChangeProperty(["NAME:AllTabs", ["NAME:LocalVariableTab", ["NAME:PropServers", "LocalVariables"], ["NAME:ChangedProps", ["NAME:patch_l", ["NAME:Optimization", "Included:=", True, "Min:=", "27mm", "Max:=", "31mm"]]]]]). Tuning (Optimetrics > Tune) is interactive; from a script use derivatives or a parametric sweep instead.

tools.name: hfss.export_parametric_results / hfss.export_results
tools.description: Bulk result export after Optimetrics or plain solves: export_parametric_results writes the variation table with all calculations of a parametric setup to CSV, and export_results dumps every available report, the profile, convergence and Touchstone files for all (or chosen) variations into a folder with configurable Touchstone formatting - a one-call archive of a solved design.
tools.usage:
hfss.export_parametric_results(setup, output_file, export_units=True)
files = hfss.export_results(export_folder=None, matrix_name="Original", matrix_type="S", touchstone_format="MagPhase",
                            touchstone_number_precision=15, length="1meter", impedance=50, include_gamma_comment=True,
                            support_non_standard_touchstone_extension=False, variations=None)

parameters.name: setup
parameters.description: Parametric setup name.

parameters.name: export_units
parameters.description: Include units in the CSV values.

parameters.name: export_folder
parameters.description: Destination folder (working directory by default).

parameters.name: matrix_type / touchstone_format / impedance
parameters.description: S/Y/Z; MagPhase, DbPhase or RealImag; reference impedance for the Touchstone files.

parameters.name: variations
parameters.description: List of variation strings to export; None exports all solved variations.

parameters.name: return
parameters.description: List of exported file paths.

tools.example:
hfss.export_parametric_results("LengthSweep", "C:/work/LengthSweep.csv", export_units=True)
files = hfss.export_results(export_folder="C:/work/results", touchstone_format="RealImag", touchstone_number_precision=12)
print(len(files), files[:3])
tools.notes: Native: oModule("Optimetrics").ExportParametricResults(setup, file, bOutputUnits); for reports oModule("ReportSetup").ExportToFile and oModule("Solutions").ExportNetworkData per variation. Field data are not included; use export_field_file for those.

tools.name: hfss.create_sbr_chirp_i_doppler_setup / create_sbr_chirp_iq_doppler_setup / create_sbr_pulse_doppler_setup / create_sbr_radar_from_json
tools.description: SBR+ radar helpers: create Doppler (range-Doppler) setups for a chirp-I, chirp-IQ or pulsed radar waveform, deriving the frequency sweep, ray density and bounces from radar parameters (centre frequency, range resolution and period, velocity resolution and span), and optionally a parametric sweep over a time variable that moves the scene (Move It extension); create_sbr_radar_from_json builds a full radar (antennas, positions, waveform) from a JSON description. The results are processed with the FRTM/range-Doppler plotting classes.
tools.usage:
setup, sweep = hfss.create_sbr_chirp_i_doppler_setup(time_variable=None, sweep_time_duration=0.0, center_freq=76.5, resolution=1,
                                                     period=200, velocity_resolution=0.4, min_velocity=-20, max_velocity=20,
                                                     ray_density_per_wavelength=0.2, max_bounces=5, include_coupling_effects=False,
                                                     doppler_ad_sampling_rate=20, setup=None)
setup, sweep = hfss.create_sbr_chirp_iq_doppler_setup(...)      # same arguments
setup, sweep = hfss.create_sbr_pulse_doppler_setup(time_variable=None, sweep_time_duration=0.0, center_freq=76.5, resolution=1,
                                                   period=200, velocity_resolution=0.4, min_velocity=-20, max_velocity=20,
                                                   ray_density_per_wavelength=0.2, max_bounces=5, setup=None)
radar = hfss.create_sbr_radar_from_json(radar_file, name, offset=None, speed=0.0, use_relative_cs=False, relative_cs_name=None)

parameters.name: center_freq
parameters.description: Radar centre frequency in GHz (76.5 for automotive).

parameters.name: resolution / period
parameters.description: Range resolution and unambiguous range in metres; they set the bandwidth and frequency step.

parameters.name: velocity_resolution / min_velocity / max_velocity
parameters.description: Doppler axis definition in m/s.

parameters.name: time_variable / sweep_time_duration
parameters.description: Design variable driving object motion and the duration over which a parametric time sweep is generated.

parameters.name: radar_file
parameters.description: JSON with antenna types, positions, tx/rx assignments and waveform for create_sbr_radar_from_json.

tools.example:
hfss = Hfss(solution_type="SBR+")
hfss["time_var"] = "0s"
hfss.modeler.import_3d_cad("C:/cad/car.step", create_lightweight_part=True)
radar = hfss.create_sbr_radar_from_json("C:/work/radar_77GHz.json", name="Radar1", offset=[0, 0, 0.5])
setup, sweep = hfss.create_sbr_chirp_iq_doppler_setup(time_variable="time_var", sweep_time_duration=0.2, center_freq=77,
                                                       resolution=0.5, period=150, velocity_resolution=0.25,
                                                       min_velocity=-30, max_velocity=30, max_bounces=3)
hfss.analyze(sweep.name if sweep else setup.name)
tools.notes: Requires the SBR+ solution type and HFSS SBR+ licensing; the Doppler post-processing (range-Doppler maps) is done from exported FRTM data with ansys.aedt.core.visualization.advanced.frtm_visualization (FRTMData / FRTMPlotter). GUI: HFSS > Analysis > Add Doppler Setup (SBR+).

tools.name: hfss.set_sbr_txrx_settings / set_sbr_current_sources_options / get_hdm_plotter / parse_hdm_file (SBR+ options and ray visualisation)
tools.description: SBR+-specific controls: set_sbr_txrx_settings declares which antenna sources transmit and which receive (the TX/RX table used for coupling and radar), set_sbr_current_sources_options tunes how linked-antenna current sources are represented (conformance, thin sources, power fraction), and parse_hdm_file / get_hdm_plotter read the .hdm ray-trace export of an SBR+ or creeping-wave solve for Visual Ray Trace inspection in PyVista.
tools.usage:
hfss.set_sbr_txrx_settings(txrx_settings)          # {"TX1": "RX1", ...} or {tx: [rx, ...]}
hfss.set_sbr_current_sources_options(conformance=False, thin_sources=False, power_fraction=0.95)
parser = hfss.parse_hdm_file(file_name)
plotter = hfss.get_hdm_plotter(file_name=None)
plotter.add_rays(...); plotter.plot_rays(...)

parameters.name: txrx_settings
parameters.description: Mapping of transmitter antenna names to receiver antenna names.

parameters.name: conformance / thin_sources / power_fraction
parameters.description: Current-source representation options for linked antennas.

parameters.name: file_name
parameters.description: Path to the .hdm file written by the SBR+ setup when ray export is enabled (Visual Ray Trace).

tools.example:
hfss.set_sbr_txrx_settings({"TX1": "RX1", "TX2": "RX1"})
hfss.set_sbr_current_sources_options(conformance=True, thin_sources=True, power_fraction=0.98)
hfss.analyze()
plotter = hfss.get_hdm_plotter("C:/work/rays.hdm")
plotter.plot_rays()
tools.notes: GUI equivalents live on the SBR+ setup's Advanced tab (TX/RX, ray export) and in the Visual Ray Trace panel. HDM files can be large; limit the exported bounces when only a qualitative view is needed.

tools.name: hfss.export_touchstone_on_completion / hfss.export_touchstone (variations, renormalization)
tools.description: Touchstone export controls: export_touchstone_on_completion sets the design to write .sNp files automatically after each solve (Design Settings > Export After Simulation), and export_touchstone writes one file for a given setup/sweep and variation with optional renormalisation to a real impedance and gamma/impedance comments. The set_export_touchstone method (see post-processing) fixes the file format options.
tools.usage:
hfss.export_touchstone_on_completion(export=True, output_dir=None)
path = hfss.export_touchstone(setup=None, sweep=None, output_file=None, variations=None, variations_value=None,
                              renormalization=False, impedance=None, gamma_impedance_comments=False)

parameters.name: export / output_dir
parameters.description: Enable automatic export and the target folder.

parameters.name: setup / sweep
parameters.description: Solved setup and sweep names; None uses the nominal sweep.

parameters.name: variations / variations_value
parameters.description: Parallel lists of variable names and values selecting the variation to export, e.g. ["patch_l"], ["29mm"].

parameters.name: renormalization / impedance
parameters.description: Renormalise to the given real impedance (50 if None).

parameters.name: gamma_impedance_comments
parameters.description: Write port gamma and impedance as comments in the file.

tools.example:
hfss.export_touchstone_on_completion(True, output_dir="C:/work/snp")
hfss.analyze()
for l in ["27mm", "29mm", "31mm"]:
    hfss.export_touchstone(setup="Setup1", sweep="Sweep1", output_file=f"C:/work/snp/patch_{l}.s1p",
                           variations=["patch_l"], variations_value=[l], renormalization=True, impedance=50)
tools.notes: Native: oModule("Solutions").ExportNetworkData(variationKey, ["Setup1:Sweep1"], 3, file, ["all"], True, 50, "S", -1, 0, 15, True, True, True). Interpolating sweeps export the fitted data at the requested points; Discrete sweeps only the solved points.

tools.name: Desktop.get_monitor_data / hfss.get_monitor_data / Desktop.analyze_all
tools.description: Session-level solve helpers: analyze_all solves every design and setup of the active (or named) project, and get_monitor_data returns the state of the running analysis - the same information as the Progress and Monitor windows (current pass, elapsed time, memory, machine) - which non-blocking runs poll to report progress or to abort on excessive memory use.
tools.usage:
hfss.desktop_class.analyze_all(project=None, design=None)
info = hfss.get_monitor_data()          # dict with per-solve progress, or {} when idle
hfss.are_there_simulations_running
hfss.stop_simulations(clean_stop=True)

parameters.name: project / design
parameters.description: Restrict analyze_all to one project or design; None = active project, all designs.

parameters.name: clean_stop
parameters.description: True lets the current step finish and keeps partial results; False aborts immediately.

tools.example:
hfss.analyze("Setup1", blocking=False)
import time
while hfss.are_there_simulations_running:
    m = hfss.get_monitor_data()
    print(m)
    time.sleep(60)
print("solved:", hfss.get_setup("Setup1").is_solved)
tools.notes: Native: oProject.AnalyzeAll() and oDesign.AnalyzeAll(); the monitor data has no simple native call - PyAEDT reads it through the ChildObject API of the running solve. blocking=False requires AEDT 2023 R2 or later.

tools.name: hfss.cleanup_solution / hfss.delete_setup / hfss.generate_unique_setup_name
tools.description: Result and setup housekeeping: cleanup_solution deletes solution data for all or selected variations (optionally keeping the mesh or linked data), which is the scripted Results > Clean Up Solutions; delete_setup removes an analysis setup and its sweeps; generate_unique_setup_name returns a setup name that does not clash with existing ones for scripts that add setups repeatedly.
tools.usage:
hfss.cleanup_solution(variations="All", entire_solution=True, field=True, mesh=True, linked_data=True)
hfss.delete_setup(name)
name = hfss.generate_unique_setup_name(name=None)

parameters.name: variations
parameters.description: "All" or a list of variation strings to clean.

parameters.name: entire_solution
parameters.description: True removes matrix data and fields (DeleteFullVariation); False removes only fields (DeleteFieldVariation).

parameters.name: field / mesh / linked_data
parameters.description: Which parts to delete when entire_solution is False.

tools.example:
hfss.cleanup_solution(variations="All", entire_solution=False, field=True, mesh=False)   # keep mesh, drop fields
hfss.delete_setup("ScratchSetup")
new = hfss.create_setup(hfss.generate_unique_setup_name("Setup"))
tools.notes: Native: oDesign.DeleteFullVariation(["All"], False), oDesign.DeleteFieldVariation(["All"], True, False, False), oModule("AnalysisSetup").DeleteSetups([name]). Cleaning solutions does not shrink the .aedtresults folder until the project is saved.

tools.name: Hfss.create_setup(setup_type="HFSSDrivenAuto") - Auto solver setup (SetupHFSSAuto)
tools.description: The HFSS Auto ("Driven Auto") setup lets HFSS choose adaptive frequencies, passes and sweep strategy from a single Fast/Balanced/Accurate preference and a frequency range, and returns a SetupHFSSAuto object. It is the recommended starting point for broadband S-parameter extraction of interconnects and packages when the engineer does not want to tune adaptation settings; the classic HFSSDriven setup remains the choice when explicit control is needed.
tools.usage:
setup = hfss.create_setup("AutoSetup", setup_type="HFSSDrivenAuto", AutoSolverSetting="Balanced",
                          Type="Discrete", RangeType="LinearCount", RangeStart="1GHz", RangeEnd="10GHz", RangeCount="501")

parameters.name: AutoSolverSetting
parameters.description: "Fast", "Balanced" or "Accurate" - trades passes and interpolation tolerance against speed.

parameters.name: Type / RangeType / RangeStart / RangeEnd / RangeCount
parameters.description: The sweep embedded in the auto setup (Discrete or Interpolating over a linear/log range).

parameters.name: SetupHFSSAuto
parameters.description: Object with the same interface as SetupHFSS (props, update, analyze, sweeps) but auto-specific properties.

tools.example:
hfss = Hfss(solution_type="Terminal")
auto = hfss.create_setup("AutoSetup", setup_type="HFSSDrivenAuto", AutoSolverSetting="Accurate",
                         RangeType="LinearCount", RangeStart="0.1GHz", RangeEnd="20GHz", RangeCount="1001")
auto.analyze(cores=8)
hfss.export_touchstone(setup="AutoSetup")
tools.notes: Native: oModule.InsertSetup("HfssDrivenAuto", ["NAME:AutoSetup", "IsEnabled:=", True, ["NAME:MeshLink", ...], "AutoSolverSetting:=", "Balanced", ["NAME:Sweeps", ["NAME:Sweep", "RangeType:=", "LinearCount", "RangeStart:=", "1GHz", "RangeEnd:=", "10GHz", "RangeCount:=", 501, "AutoSolverSetting:=", "Balanced", "Type:=", "Discrete"]]]). Auto setups are only available in Driven Modal/Terminal designs.
